result:
1. Commit numeric HALT thresholds before spend; never defer to "reassess if it looks bad."
2. Include a same-input churn arm with a numeric floor for designs scoring per-item presence/absence across LLM redraws; treat "effect inside churn floor" as a valid outcome, not a failure; note n=1 drift runs are anti-conservative and n=2 gives only a floor, not an estimate.
3. Ensure outcome tables are total and rows partition the full outcome space; check totality, two-sidedness, n-consistency, and non-degeneracy at the given n.
4. Explicitly write NULL-composite rows for every arm that can read NULL, rather than deciding null handling after seeing the data.
5. Apply two-sided calibration to every gate: verify it fires on a planted violation and stays quiet on the clean case.
6. Pre-register selection rules for controls, including the RNG seed, before the arm they select on runs, with an explicit skip-as-moot branch.
7. Classify the cause of kill-condition failures when more than one cause with different correct responses could trigger them; write this classification step into the prereg.
8. Pin an effect-size floor (magnitude/share above uniform expectation) before computing any grid value, rather than relying on α; report the small stratum's MDE alongside it; if MDE doesn't clear the floor, treat the condition as not a falsifier and stop.
9. Report a failed locked metric as failed, full stop; then pose a new pre-registered question keyed on a quantity unobserved at lock time, rather than retrofitting a metric that passes.
10. Fire recon gates interactively, surfacing each to the operator at fire time with its witness and pre-committed branch, rather than post-hoc in the writeup.
11. Make freeze ordering witnessable: write PREREGISTRATION.md, md5sum it into audit_log.md above the first result, then run; show both md5s with positions on amendment.
12. Split tolerance by indicator kind (consumer safety vs. process quality) and whether firing is systemic or idiosyncratic, rather than using one aggregate tolerance for both.
13. Ensure churn/discount rules cover every payload-carrying file, not just one file standing in for all.
